title: Zenith Payments opportunity notebook
content:
Quick notes and scratch ideas for Zenith Payments outreach (raw, iterative).

Background snapshot (quick):
- Company: Zenith Payments (mid-market, B2B payments processor). HQ: Atlanta. ~450 employees. Raised Series D in 2024.
- Why they matter: large merchant base (retail + ecommerce), latency-sensitive fraud checks, on-prem adapters for regulated bank partners. Potential win: platform licensing + dedicated capacity for predictable throughput across settlement windows.
- Public signals: hiring for "platform reliability" and "ml infra" roles in Q2 2025; posted job requiring experience with "vector search" and "low-latency inference".

Key stakeholders (persona map):
- VP Product: Elena Costa — owns product roadmap, cares about developer DX, time-to-market for new features.
- Head of Infrastructure: Daniel Park — gate for any infra/hosting changes, cares about security, isolation, cost per request, and auditability.
- ML Platform Lead: Tamika Rivers — interested in model ops, evals, and quality tracking for fraud models.
- Procurement / Legal: negotiates data residency, indemnities, and SLAs.

Initial hypotheses on needs & pain: 
- They run a hybrid stack (cloud + colocated for some bank partners). Likely lack consolidated inference routing and A/B rollouts across environments.
- Fraud scoring needs consistent low tail latency during peak settlement; current approach is brittle (multiple model variants across teams).
- Sensitive data + PCI scope makes Private/VPC or on-prem options a strong fit.
- Are cost-conscious — sensitive to per-transaction cost if millions of daily decisions.

Value props to stress (tailored):
- Prediction economics: show unit-cost math for fraud model serving with Redwood Optimize (batching, kv cache). Example: 2x throughput at 0.6x cost with conservative batching + 4-bit quantization on dedicated instances.
- Predictable SLAs and isolation: Redwood Dedicated or Private meets PCI scoped environments, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs.
- Unified rollout + fallback: can route requests to cheaper model variants during high load without manual changes to their infra; reduces incident blast radius.
- Observability for trust: token-level tracing and eval hooks to monitor model drift/regressions (valuable for ML ops + compliance).

Questions to validate in discovery: 
- Which models are latency-critical? (fraud scoring, auth decisions, customer-facing chat?)
- Current request volume distribution (p95, p99 latency targets).
- Data residency / PCI scope: what systems are in-scope today?
- Do they already use private VPC endpoints for other vendors? If yes, what's the onboarding time?
- Who owns procurement / security checklist? SLA negotiation expectations?

Potential objections and counters (quick):
- "We already built our own infra / in-house model serving."
  - Counter: acknowledge investment; show cost of maintenance + feature gaps (rollouts, canary, unified observability). Offer a hybrid model: Redwood Private control plane with on-prem workers to keep data in-scope while offloading orchestration.
- "PCI/regulatory concerns — can't send tokens offsite."
  - Counter: Redwood Private + HSM/KMS integration, on-prem package, attestations. Offer to map their specific compliance checklist in a short session and provide a compliance runbook.
- "Cost — per-transaction fees add up."
  - Counter: Redwood Optimize + batching/kv cache can reduce token compute significantly; provide a sample TCO spreadsheet comparing self-host vs Redwood Dedicated with projected 12-month spend.
- "Lock-in concerns with custom infra."
  - Counter: emphasize model versioning and ability to export models / run locally; also show how routing policies are transparent and reversible.

Outbound messaging drafts (short + long). Use as A/B for initial touch: 
- Cold email subject A: "Reduce fraud-model latency without re-architecting infra"
  Body (short):
  Hi Elena —

  Quick note: saw ZenPay's listings for platform reliability hires and thought it might be timely. Redwood helps payments teams cut tail latency and unit cost for real-time models (fraud, auth) while preserving PCI isolation — we do this with dedicated pools and a private deployment option.

  If helpful, I can share a short 20-min sketch of how we map to your peak-window economics and a sample TCO vs self-hosting. When's a good time next week?

  Thanks,
  Maya

- Cold email subject B (more technical): "Can your fraud team meet 99.9th% latency targets at peak?"
  Body (short):
  Hi Elena —

  Quick question: what's your p99 target for fraud scoring during settlement peaks? We recently helped a payments customer drop p99 by ~40% with lambda batching + KV cache and saved ~30% on serving cost. Happy to walk through the pattern and a proof-of-concept plan.

  Best,
  Maya

- LinkedIn intro (brief):
  Hi Elena — small note from someone at Redwood Inference. We help payments platforms reduce inference cost/latency while keeping data in customer-controlled networks. Would love to share a quick example relevant to fraud scoring — open to 15 mins?

Meeting agenda (first discovery call — 30m):
- 5m: intros + decision process overview
- 10m: technical constraints (latency targets, p99, traffic profile, infra topology)
- 7m: Redwood quick sketch (Dedicated vs Private, routing, fallback)
- 5m: compliance & procurement checklist items
- 3m: next steps / POC ask (sample data volume + timeline)

POC ideas (light weight):
- 2-week sandbox: run a replication of fraud scoring traffic to Redwood Dedicated pool on a smaller commit; measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 100k decisions. Provide a short eval harness and automated regression checks.
- Minimal data access: use synthetic or obfuscated logs; Redwood can accept model artifacts and run load locally to avoid sending sensitive customer data.

Internal asks / playbook notes: 
- Ask SRE partner (Arjun) for a strawman cost model for Dedicated with 4x batch windows; include cold-start and warmup notes.
- Ask Product SWE (Sofia) for a short write-up of the migration path for their auth pipeline (how we integrate with existing request flows).
- Legal: prep a compliance mapping document comparing Redwood Private controls to Zenith's PCI checklist.

Metrics / win criteria (for our internal evaluation):
- p99 latency improvement >= 20% in pilot
- Serving cost per decision reduction >= 15% compared to baseline or clearer justification (e.g., reduced ops overhead)
- Fast onboarding (sandbox in <= 2 weeks)

Hypothetical commercial framework (rough):
- Starter pilot: 3-month sandbox, nominal commit to cover reserved capacity ($Xk/mo) — include support + onboarding credits.
- Scale: 12-month Dedicated with tiered throughput pricing and optional Private deployment fee.

Next steps (immediate):
- Send Elena short intro (A/B test email A then B if no response) — target window: Mon/Tue morning next week.
- Prep short one-pager (2 slides) comparing Redwood Dedicated vs DIY for fraud workloads (ops cost, latency, compliance). Draft owner: Maya, with Arjun for cost numbers.
- Set 1:1 with Arjun (tomorrow) to estimate infra sizing for pilot.

Loose brainstorming / scribbles:
- Could propose co-branded whitepaper on "Operationalizing fraud models in regulated payments" if they have content interest — opens exec engagement.
- Risk: procurement at Zenith tends to push for longer RFP cycles; need an internal champion to accelerate.
- Consider involving Solutions Eng early to demo live routing and fallback flows (shows immediate value).

Notes to self: keep messages short & concrete; call out PCI and p99 immediately in subject/preview. Track outreach cadence in CRM and tag as "Zenith-2025-pilot".

---
End of scratchpad. Save as working doc; will iterate after first call.
